data.title: Clone
data.tagline: Create a local copy of a remote repository and its history
data.description: Clone downloads a repository, creates a working directory, and configures the original location as a remote. It is normally the first step when joining an existing project. Check the destination path and repository source before running it.

use: Start work on an existing repository
Create a fresh local working copy
Set up the default remote automatically
avoid: Clone into a directory that already contains important files
Download code from an untrusted source and run it immediately
Clone again every time the remote changes
Assume private dependencies and environment settings are included

lessonPractice.title: A new teammate needs a local copy of a GitHub project, including its code and version history. How should they begin?

options.label: Clone the correct repository, enter the new directory, read README, and install from project configuration
options.feedback: Clone retrieves code and history, setup follows project guidance, and later updates use Pull.

options.label: Download and unzip an archive and treat it as a repository with complete Git history
options.feedback: An archive generally contains a file snapshot without branches, commit history, or remote connection.

options.label: Clone again for every update and distinguish versions through folder names
options.feedback: Repeated downloads create inconsistent workspaces; an existing repository should use Pull.

data.agentPrompt: Clone the provided repository into one clearly named new directory, then inspect README, package configuration, and environment examples before installing and starting. Verify remote and branch; use Pull for later synchronization.
